flashcard_questions.q: What does the law of conservation of mass state?
flashcard_questions.a: The total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is mass always conserved in a chemical reaction?
flashcard_questions.a: No atoms are created or destroyed; they are only rearranged.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does the balance reading fall when calcium carbonate reacts with acid?
flashcard_questions.a: Carbon dioxide gas is produced and escapes from the open container.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does the balance reading rise when magnesium burns in air?
flashcard_questions.a: Oxygen atoms from the air combine with the metal, adding mass.

flashcard_questions.q: When balancing an equation, which numbers are you allowed to change?
flashcard_questions.a: Only the large coefficients written in front of the formulae.

flashcard_questions.q: How is the relative formula mass of a compound calculated?
flashcard_questions.a: Add the relative atomic masses of every atom shown in its formula.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the relative formula mass of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃?
What is the value of Avogadro's constant?
Which equation links moles, mass and relative formula mass?
Rearrange the moles equation to make mass the subject.
How many moles are there in 11 g of CO₂, where Mr is 44?
What is the limiting reactant in a chemical reaction?
flashcard_questions.a: The reactant used up first, which fixes how much product can form.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens once the limiting reactant has been used up?
flashcard_questions.a: The reaction stops, even if plenty of the other reactant remains.

flashcard_questions.q: Which equation gives the concentration of a solution in g/dm³?
flashcard_questions.a: Concentration = mass of solute ÷ volume of solution.

flashcard_questions.q: How many cm³ are there in 1 dm³?
